Text.Text: Look at that turn. You carry the eye with you now -- the students copy your footwork when they think I'm not watching. The halls are open, the form has a center again, and I have nothing left to teach you that the staff won't say better.
Keep walking. Your feet stop every time your hands get busy. Reach rank 50 in Saberstaff, then come back. I want both ends of you ready for this.

Six Saber Cyclone adepts have sealed the Enclave Trial Halls. They've practiced the turn so long they've forgotten where it takes them. Beat the six and bring me their enclave slate. I want to see whether any of the footwork survived.
The key opens the Trial Halls entrance in the Enclave Library. Go rested. If your feet are dragging now, they'll be dragging when you need them.

Most forms plant their feet and swing. The cyclone never plants. The staff keeps turning -- every parry feeds the next arc, defense becomes orbit, and whatever steps into the orbit gets carried out of it. What they're doing down there is all spin and no center. You'll learn the difference by unmaking theirs.
The Trial Halls entrance is in the Jedi Enclave Library on Dantooine. My key opens it. Have your companions beside you when you enter; the halls needn't separate you.

Adepts who've drilled the cyclone's opening turns until they're reflex. Reflex without judgment cuts in both directions -- they won't stop at first blood, because nobody taught them where a drill ends. Don't extend your arcs to impress them. Six, cleanly, and out.
Six adepts in the Enclave Trial Halls. Bring their slate here to Dantooine Interior. Keep your feet moving before the blades need them.
There -- your arcs came back shorter. The halls did that in a day; imagine a year. And that's the slate under your arm. Hand it over.

Six adepts and their drill slate. Want to know what's wrong with it? Nothing. Every form on it is copied perfectly -- that's the lesson. Perfect copies, no center. The credits are for your time. The next turn is faster.

Five specialists have built their practice around a kyber shard in the Trial Halls. They're letting it set their pace. Beat the five and bring it here. If you catch yourself matching their rhythm, break your own first.
Bring the shard back wrapped. And keep your feet working when they start trying to set your pace.

Kyber holds a note when you feed it attention. The specialists use the shard as a false center -- focus on the stone and the cyclone feels effortless, right up until the stone isn't there. It's a crutch dressed as a doctrine. That's why it comes out of the halls and into my hand.
The Trial Halls entrance is in the Jedi Enclave Library on Dantooine. My key opens it. Have your companions beside you when you enter; the halls needn't separate you.

Better than the adepts, and worse. The shard smooths their gaps, so they're flawless until you break their tempo -- then they stumble over their own orbit. Change your speed and keep changing it. And they spar live steel down there, so treat every exchange as real. It is.
Five specialists in the Trial Halls have the kyber shard. Bring it here after they're beaten.
I can hear it from here. Even wrapped, that shard hums like it's mid-drill. You outlasted five teachers at their own tempo -- give it over.

Listen to it. Kyber sings whatever you feed it, and they fed it certainty for a year. You heard the difference; they never did. Take your pay, walk the long way back, and let your arms argue about what they learned.

The warden is holding the Trial Halls. Challenge him there and bring back his fractured sigil when he's beaten. Take companions who can keep moving. He'll be pleased if you all stop in the same place.

Then hear the rest at walking pace. He fights the ring like it's his orbit, because it is -- don't take turns with him. Overlap him: one draws the arc, one breaks it, one finishes. That's why you're bringing company. Sigil off his belt, and come back standing.

He graded my students for twenty years. He graded me, once -- passed me, which I've held against him ever since. Somewhere in the scoring he stopped seeing duelists and started seeing gaps. Whatever he says to you mid-fight, don't answer. He's counting the syllables you waste.
Use the challenge marker in the Enclave Trial Halls. That calls the warden. Go rested and fed. He wants challengers, especially tired ones.
He waits well. Very little chasing, very little wasted motion. If you let him set every turn, you'll tire before he does. Bring help if you can, and keep choosing where your feet go.
Call the warden at the Trial Halls challenge marker. Beat him and recover the fractured sigil.
You walked back up the stairs -- I know because the students stopped whispering about the ring an hour ago. Sigil first. Then breathe.

Cracked down the middle. He did that himself the day he decided his orbit was the standard everything else fell short of. I'll set it back where the masters' mark belongs, crack and all -- some lessons should stay visible. You did this the right way: not alone. Keep that shape. You'll need it once more.

Four council keepers still have the trial chit. They've approved every turn of this school without leaving their own circle. Defeat the four in the halls and bring it here. We'll see what they put their names to.
Recover the trial chit. Keep moving while they decide which part of their circle to defend.

The warden's chosen -- the four he scored highest. Each one built their cyclone around a different lie: speed, reach, endurance, fury. Together they cover one another's gaps, which is the only true thing he ever taught them.
The four keepers are still in the Trial Halls. They know their warden fell. Keep your feet working; they'll be waiting for you to stop.

Four cyclones that learned to orbit each other. Split them if you can. If you can't, bring enough blades that splitting stops mattering. And watch the one who hangs back -- the warden always graded patience highest.
Four council keepers in the Trial Halls have the trial chit. Bring it back when you've broken their circle.
The chamber went quiet yesterday -- the whole enclave felt it. You're carrying the chit like it's heavier than it looks. It is. Give it here.

Sealed and unspent. They held the council's proof for a year and never once earned the right to open it. You've earned it four times over. The halls reopen, the council owes me a favor, and I lose my best excuse for walking fast. One trial left -- and I've been avoiding saying her name.

My old master is in the Saber Trial Chamber. Call her at the challenge marker and defeat her. She knows the cyclone better than I do. That doesn't mean you should let her decide where your feet go. Come back and we'll walk through what happened.

Then the last part, plainly, standing still: her orbit widens as she tires. Most people back away from it -- that's when she takes them. Step in when everyone else would step out. That's the whole secret, and it took me twenty years and one empty chair to learn it. Come back, and I'll finish your sentence one last time.

She was the best center I ever saw. Still, kind, certain -- then the turning became the center, and the rest of her went into it. What's down there remembers every form and none of the reasons. If she speaks, it will sound like me on my best day. It isn't me. It's the form, talking to itself.
The Saber Trial Chamber. Use the challenge marker there to call her. She knows the halls have gone quiet, and she'll be watching how you enter.

Both blades moving, nothing wasted, very little spared. Watch your footing before you watch hers. I'd take companions if you can; she knows how to keep a lone challenger turning until there's nowhere left to go.
Call the master in the Saber Trial Chamber. Beat her, then meet me here. We'll keep walking while you tell me.
The halls are quiet all the way to the bottom. I walked down to the ring this morning just to listen. I know already -- say it anyway. I want the words.
She stopped, and you kept moving. I hoped you'd find a way. Take your pay. If you want to learn Saber Cyclone from me, we'll start where we always should have: with the next step.
Keep walking. Tell me the trial again.
Six adepts and the slate. Point me at the stairs.
What is the cyclone, exactly?
Where do I find these adepts?
What am I walking into?
Not yet. My footing isn't there.
The Saber Cyclone Enclave Trial Slate. Take it.
Slow down -- the specialists. Go over it again.
Five specialists. The shard comes back with me.
What does the shard actually do?
Where do the specialists train?
How do they fight?
Not this turn. Give me a day.
The Saber Cyclone Kyber Focus Shard. It hasn't stopped humming.
Tell me what you want done again.
I'll bring the blades. The warden falls.
Who is this warden?
Where is the trial ring?
What will he throw at us?
My blades aren't here yet. Soon.
The Saber Cyclone Fractured Trial Sigil. The ring is open.
Back to the four. I'm listening.
Four duelists, one chit. Done.
Who are the inner circle?
Where are they holed up?
How do the four fight together?
When my edge comes back. Not before.
The Saber Cyclone Council Trial Chit. The chamber is quiet.
Start over. I want to hear all of it again.
I'll call her out. It ends there.
What did she become?
Where does she wait?
What should we expect from her?
Not until my people are ready. She can wait.
She's defeated. The cyclone has a center again.
